grouping_rule: Same frozen source path plus same semantic standing only; R22P0121 uses effective SOURCE_ASSERTION_CONCEPTUAL standing.
items: Evolution log records the conceptual evolution of a source-named Constraint–Trajectory Coupling (CTC) framework.
Evolution sequence includes causal mass, Causal Permeability E*->C_rev, closed/open revision, K-vs-causal-graph distinction, Omega->Delta mathcal G and R->Omega->C->A->R' recursive cycle.
Source says causal importance is counterfactual world difference and identifies reality's access to future-change mechanism as a missing variable for open adaptation.
Trajectory changes inside possibility space; lineage allows reality to reshape it.
Evolution log describes semantic-collision relabeling test of whether names alter mechanism.
Source-reported conceptual outcome: relabeling changed K but not G; source concludes names are coordinates and relations are structure. No empirical standing is inferred.
Evolution log converges on causal accessibility E*->C_rev as the preserved invariant for open-endedness.
Current research direction is explicitly described as empirical testing of causal permeability against generalization, reachability, shift robustness and recursive improvement.

basic_experiment.py implements an intended closed-vs-permeable demo, imports runner primitives, constructs shared environment/simulators, computes named scores and conditionally prints interpretation labels.
Example predicts permeable mechanism-space/shift/residual advantage, not necessarily immediate strength.
export_results.py provides JSON/CSV result/history export utilities and metadata packaging for supplied experiment objects.
Export script main block contains hard-coded illustrative histories/metrics and calls them first_ctc_run.
plot_results.py plots supplied closed/permeable capability and mechanism-expansion series and optionally saves a figure.
Plot docstring predicts greater reachable-mechanism growth for permeable condition if the experiment works.
Plot main block explicitly uses placeholder sample histories showing permeable growth.
YAML config names CTC benchmark, sets 100x500 scale/seed/environment/agent/CTC-variable/metric/output parameters and requests result/plot artifacts.
run_ctc_benchmark.py explicitly says it is an experimental protocol, not proof of CTC.
Benchmark runner imports expected agent/metric APIs, has local 20x100 defaults, runs shared-environment closed/permeable trials, aggregates adaptation means and can save JSON summaries.
run_from_config.py describes config-separated execution and calls target a Causal Permeability Principle benchmark while retaining CTC hypothesis.
Config runner loads YAML, consumes trials/steps/difficulties/output directory, delegates to run_trial/summarize_results and writes results/summary JSON.
requirements header labels project Causal Permeability Principle computational validation framework.
Dependencies: pyyaml, numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scipy, pytest and tqdm.
.gitignore excludes Python/build/test/editor artifacts and normal generated results/, figures/, logs, CSV/JSON outputs, with example-data exceptions.

ctc_core.py implements ConstraintSignal, mutable mechanism list, revision rules, treatment-switch CTCController, deterministic source-named mechanism generation, AdaptiveAgent delegation, switch-based permeability proxy and mechanism-space-size comparison.
environment.py implements EnvironmentState, mutable Environment, observation/constraint extraction, perturbations and toy benchmark factories.

metrics.py implements treatment-state permeability, list-size mechanism expansion, adaptation velocity, residual/dependency arithmetic and a multiplicative CTC composite with textual threshold interpretations.
simulator.py implements simulation state/step/run/evaluate/comparison functions, expecting adapt-result capability/mechanisms and using synthetic removal/dependency inputs in evaluation.
tests/test_ctc.py explicitly says tests represent the hypothesis but do not prove CTC true.
Test source defines ClosedAgent/PermeableAgent mocks expecting capability/mechanism/result APIs and can invoke pytest directly.
Five pytest protocols target environmental access, mechanism expansion, closed-vs-permeable comparison, causal cut and Omega-causes-generator-change hypothesis.
